rationale: I read the complete held EO 14228 (90 FR 11463, March 3, 2025): sec. 1 background, sec. 2 its only operative command, amending sec. 2(a) of EO 14195 (PRC synthetic-opioid tariffs) by striking '10 percent' and inserting '20 percent', and sec. 3 general provisions; no own sunset or savings clause. I read the complete held EO 14389 (91 FR 9437, Feb. 20, 2026, Ending Certain Tariff Actions). Sec. 1 says that 'the additional ad valorem duties imposed pursuant to IEEPA in ... Executive Order 14195, as amended ... shall no longer be in effect and, as soon as practicable, shall no longer be collected', sec. 2(a) directs agencies to end those duties, and sec. 2(d) confines the order to the additional IEEPA duties. The duties 'imposed ... in Executive Order 14195, as amended' include the 20 percent rate that is the whole operative content of EO 14228, so that rate no longer has effect, and EO 14228 has no other command to survive; sec. 1 preserves other actions only if they 'do not impose additional ad valorem duties'. The 'as amended' phrase reaches EO 14228 without naming it, and EO 14389 says the national emergencies remain in effect, so the basis is the termination of the duty effect, not a revocation of the order text. Residual risks: EO 14389 gives no single effective date ('as soon as practicable'); de minimis suspensions that cite EO 14228 (EO 14256, EO 14324) were examined only through the quoted passage and are separate orders; the catalog cross-references to EO 14200 and EO 14256 are not endings. The held EO 14324 ACT passages are recitals, not an ending, and are not relied on. Provisional NO hypothesis only.
